_comment: HELIX glossary. Inline <dfn data-term="KEY">...</dfn> tags open a modal with the term's definition; the Glossary panel renders the full table. APPEND new terms anywhere — order within a category is alphabetical by convention but not required. Each entry: id (the data-term key), term (display), cat (category for table grouping), gloss (one-line, for tooltip/modal header), def (fuller, for the table).

terms.gloss: Info Noise-Contrastive Estimation — a contrastive loss whose softmax denominator HELIX reads as a partition function.
terms.def: Information Noise-Contrastive Estimation: a self-supervised loss that pulls matched (positive) pairs together and pushes mismatched (negative) pairs apart in embedding space. HELIX's central identity is that its softmax denominator IS the partition function Z, making the loss a Boltzmann distribution.

terms.gloss: Statistical-mechanics distribution p ∝ exp(−E/kT) over states by energy.
terms.def: The statistical-mechanics distribution assigning probability proportional to exp(−E/kT) across states by energy E. HELIX identifies the InfoNCE softmax with this form, which is what lets Jaynes' maximum-entropy program govern the embedding objective.

terms.gloss: The normalizing denominator of a Boltzmann/softmax distribution.
terms.def: The normalizing sum Z = Σ exp(−E/T) over all states in a Boltzmann distribution. It is the bridge object in HELIX: the InfoNCE denominator, the Bayesian evidence at unit temperature, and the spine connecting the embedding, background, and epistemic goals.

terms.gloss: The InfoNCE scale parameter; τ = 1/β, the inverse entropy scale.
terms.def: The InfoNCE scale parameter. In the thermodynamic reading τ = 1/β, the inverse temperature, controlling how sharply the distribution concentrates. Lowering τ sharpens the contrast; raising it softens it.

terms.gloss: "Event to vector" — a Word2Vec/skip-gram analogue learning self-supervised event embeddings.
terms.def: The phase-1 model: an analogue of Word2Vec that learns self-supervised vector embeddings of ATLAS events from their constituent physics objects, using contrastive (InfoNCE) pretraining.

terms.gloss: Transformer encoder over the ordered cutflow sequence (phase 2).
terms.def: The phase-2 model: a transformer encoder that reads the ordered cutflow as a sequence, consuming Evt2Vec embeddings and applying attention across cut stages. Slated for the Fall build, not the summer proof of concept.

terms.gloss: The ordered sequence of selection cuts applied to events in an analysis.
terms.def: The ordered series of selection criteria ("cuts") applied to events to isolate a signal region. HELIX reads it two ways: as a sentence (cut stages as tokens) and as a thermodynamic process (each cut a prior update, the entropy drop the per-cut information gain).

terms.gloss: ATLAS's graph-neural-network flavour tagger; HELIX's published baseline for comparison.
terms.def: ATLAS's graph-neural-network-based flavour-tagging model. HELIX positions its architecture against GN2, differentiating on information-theoretic grounding and novel epistemic metrics rather than raw tagging performance.

terms.gloss: Four-axis Robust Ranking Metric penalty vector — a principled model-selection / stopping criterion.
terms.def: A four-component penalty vector extending the Robust Ranking Metric (accuracy, fold stability, posterior variance, and a fourth axis such as ABCD closure quality). It turns the MaxEnt uncertainty floor into a principled criterion for when a model has reached its epistemic limit.

terms.gloss: Maximum entropy — Jaynes' principle of the least-committal distribution consistent with known constraints.
terms.def: The maximum-entropy principle (Jaynes): given known constraints, choose the distribution with the most entropy — the least-committal one consistent with what is known. The correct MaxEnt distribution depends on the constraints (Gaussian for fixed variance, Exponential for non-negative fixed-mean, Poisson for counts).

terms.gloss: E. T. Jaynes' framework casting statistical mechanics as inference.
terms.def: E. T. Jaynes' 1957 framework showing thermodynamics is in essence a theory of information, and that statistical-mechanics tools apply to inference. It is the foundation for HELIX's MaxEnt floor and the InfoNCE-as-Boltzmann identity.

terms.gloss: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo — a gradient-guided MCMC sampler for posteriors.
terms.def: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo: a Markov-chain Monte Carlo method that uses gradient information to draw efficient samples from a posterior over weights. HELIX uses it (last-layer) to estimate epistemic uncertainty; a prior run suffered convergence collapse (low ESS), motivating the normalising-flow alternative.

terms.gloss: Data-driven background estimate from two assumed-independent variables defining four regions.
terms.def: A data-driven background-estimation technique that uses two variables, assumed uncorrelated for background, to define four regions (A, B, C, D) and predict the signal-region background from the others. HELIX's MaxEnt surprise score is a handle structurally orthogonal to the ABCD plane.

terms.gloss: Word Embedding Association Test — permutation test for differential association in an embedding.
terms.def: Word Embedding Association Test (Caliskan et al., 2017): a permutation test for whether two sets of concepts differ in their association with an attribute, measured by cosine similarity. HELIX adapts it to cross-check ABCD's independence assumption and to detect simulation-vs-data provenance artifacts.

terms.gloss: Word Embedding Factual Association Test — tests whether an embedding encodes a real-valued property.
terms.def: Word Embedding Factual Association Test (Caliskan et al., 2017): tests whether an embedding has absorbed a veridical real-valued property of the world. HELIX uses it to validate that Evt2Vec embeddings predict physical quantities (e.g. displacement, mass point), evidence the embedding learned physics.

terms.gloss: Long-Lived Particle — travels a measurable distance before decaying, giving displaced signatures.
terms.def: Long-Lived Particle: a hypothesized particle whose lifetime is long enough to traverse measurable detector distance before decaying, producing displaced (rather than prompt) decay signatures. The target of HELIX's physics application.

terms.gloss: Hidden Sector Scalar — the specific LLP signal model HELIX targets.
terms.def: Hidden Sector Scalar: the specific long-lived-particle signal model under study, in which a scalar from a hidden sector decays to produce displaced vertices in the muon spectrometer.

terms.gloss: Displaced Muon-Spectrometer Vertex — the detector signature HELIX searches for.
terms.def: Muon-Spectrometer Vertex: a decay vertex reconstructed in the ATLAS muon spectrometer, displaced from the collision point. It is the characteristic signature of the long-lived-particle decay HELIX targets.

terms.gloss: S(x) = −log p(x): the information content of an event under the background model.
terms.def: The surprisal S(x) = −log p(x): how unexpected an event is under the MaxEnt background model. Large surprise flags signal-like events. It is HELIX's neural-network-free background handle, complementary to the ABCD plane.

terms.gloss: Word2Vec scheme predicting context tokens from a center token.
terms.def: A Word2Vec training scheme that learns embeddings by predicting surrounding context tokens from a center token. Evt2Vec adapts this, treating an event's physics objects as the tokens.

terms.gloss: Self-supervised representation learning by distinguishing positive from negative pairs.
terms.def: Self-supervised learning that builds representations by distinguishing matched (positive) pairs from mismatched (negative) pairs — the family that includes InfoNCE. It needs no labels, learning structure directly from the data.

terms.gloss: A two-token model capturing first-order (adjacent) sequence structure.
terms.def: A model over adjacent token pairs, capturing only first-order sequence structure. In HELIX the bigram is not a baseline to beat but a measurement instrument: the gap between bigram and full-model performance quantifies how much discriminating power lives in higher-order structure.

terms.gloss: The assumption that the next state depends only on the current one.
terms.def: The assumption that the next element of a sequence depends only on the current one, ignoring longer-range structure. The bigram embodies it; attention (CutFormer) is meant to exceed it, and the gap between them is what HELIX measures.

terms.gloss: Converting continuous detector features into discrete tokens — the "numbers, not words" step.
terms.def: Turning continuous detector features into discrete tokens, via the pipeline StandardScaler → KBinsDiscretizer → DictVectorizer. Because HELIX has numbers rather than words, this is the core technical step on which every language-model result depends.

terms.gloss: Reducible uncertainty from incomplete knowledge or finite data (vs. aleatoric noise).
terms.def: Uncertainty arising from incomplete knowledge — finite training data, underdetermined weights, ambiguous decision boundaries — and therefore reducible with more or better data. Distinct from aleatoric (intrinsic) noise. It is what HELIX's Bayesian layer quantifies and decomposes into overall and boundary components.

terms.gloss: Per-cut-stage entropy of the MaxEnt distribution — a physics-derived lower bound on uncertainty.
terms.def: The entropy H(p_k) of the maximum-entropy distribution at each cut stage k, serving as a physics-derived lower bound on model uncertainty — a floor below which confidence cannot be justified. Epistemic error is measured against it.

terms.gloss: Posterior over only the final layer's weights, with the trunk frozen — fast, HMC-tractable.
terms.def: A configuration placing a posterior over only the output layer's weights while freezing the deterministic feature extractor. Fast enough to resample interactively while still surfacing epistemic structure at the decision boundary, where the interesting questions live.

terms.gloss: An invertible neural map between a Gaussian and a complex distribution.
terms.def: An invertible, differentiable neural network mapping a simple (Gaussian) distribution to a complex one. In HELIX it offers a sampler-free route to partition functions, evidences, and entropies — sidestepping the convergence failures of HMC (reliable through second moments).

terms.gloss: The distribution over weights/predictions given data, p(w|D); its width is epistemic uncertainty.
terms.def: The distribution p(w|D) over model weights given the data, replacing a single trained weight set. Every prediction becomes a distribution; its width is the model's epistemic uncertainty made visible — narrow means earned confidence, wide means borrowed.

terms.gloss: Temperature-dependent measure of model complexity from the Bayes-partition formalism; n_eff ≤ n.
terms.def: A temperature-dependent complexity measure from the Bayes-partition formalism (Kuntz et al., 2024), defined via the heat-capacity analogue. n_eff ≤ n, shrinking as higher-order (non-Gaussian) correlations appear — a diagnostic of how many degrees of freedom a model genuinely uses.

terms.gloss: Average surprisal of a variable; its irreducible uncertainty, in bits.
terms.def: H(x) = Σ p(x_i) log(1/p(x_i)). The mean Shannon information (surprisal) over a variable's outcomes. On detector data it is the MaxEnt floor H(p_k): the uncertainty a model is entitled to at a given cut stage and no less.

terms.gloss: Continuous analogue of entropy; meaningful only through differences.
terms.def: H(x) = ∫ p(x) log(1/p(x)) dx. The continuous-variable version of entropy (eq 32). Its absolute value is reference-dependent and formally infinite, so it is used only via differences such as mutual information — which is why MI, not raw entropy, is the safe quantity for continuous observables (displacement, mass, pT).

terms.gloss: Total uncertainty of a pair of variables taken together.
terms.def: H(x,y), the uncertainty of the joint (input, output) system. Decomposes as H(x,y) = I(x,y) + H(x|y) + H(y|x): shared information plus the two residual uncertainties (eq 35).

terms.gloss: Residual uncertainty in y once x is known; for a detector, the resolution entropy.
terms.def: H(y|x): uncertainty remaining in the output once the input is known. In the detector-as-channel picture this equals the noise entropy H(η) — the resolution / smearing introduced by reconstruction (eq 36).

terms.gloss: Uncertainty about the truth that remains after the measurement is seen.
terms.def: H(x|y): the uncertainty about the input (truth) left after observing the output (reconstructed event). It is the quantity that caps unfolding and truth inference — large equivocation means no procedure recovers truth cleanly, a fact about the data rather than the algorithm.

terms.gloss: Shared information between two variables; model-independent discriminating power.
terms.def: I(x,y) = H(x) − H(x|y) = H(y) − H(y|x), equal to the KL divergence between the joint and the product of marginals (eq 46). On detector data, I(feature; label) is the model-independent separating power of a variable: it upper-bounds any classifier built on that feature, so it ranks cut variables without committing to an architecture.

terms.gloss: Information cost of using distribution q in place of the true p.
terms.def: D_KL(p‖q) = Σ p log(p/q): the expected extra surprisal from modelling p with q. Mutual information is the special case D_KL(joint ‖ product of marginals), which is the bridge from information theory to the pyhf likelihood.

terms.gloss: Maximum information a channel can carry per use; the ceiling on detector sensitivity.
terms.def: C = max over input distributions p(x) of I(x,y) (eq 53). The most information about the underlying physics the detector can deliver per event; it is the hard upstream ceiling on how well any analysis can separate hypotheses (and thus on CLs reach). Gaussian limit: C = ½ log(1 + S/N) (eq 54).

terms.gloss: The model y = x + η: truth in, reconstructed event out, detector response as noise.
terms.def: Shannon's channel y = x + η read onto a detector: truth-level event x is the transmitted message, the reconstructed event y is what is received, and the detector response (resolution, efficiency, fakes, pileup) is the noise η. In general the response is a migration kernel R(y|x) — not additive and not Gaussian — so the discrete entropy/MI equations apply, with the Gaussian channel as a special case.

terms.gloss: Information cannot increase along a processing chain.
terms.def: For a chain truth → hits → reco → cut variables → NN score → decision, mutual information is non-increasing: I(truth;score) ≤ I(truth;reco) ≤ I(truth;hits). No downstream stage can recover information an upstream stage discarded; computing MI per stage locates where sensitivity leaks.

terms.gloss: Converting raw input into a sequence of integer token IDs from a fixed vocabulary.
terms.def: The step that turns raw input into a sequence of integer token IDs drawn from a fixed vocabulary, ready for an embedding layer. For text it is segmentation into sub-words; for continuous detector features it is quantization (binning) plus namespacing, structural tokens, and ordering.

terms.gloss: A single integer ID from the vocabulary; here, a (feature, bin) pair.
terms.def: One integer ID from the vocabulary, mapped to a learned vector by the embedding table. In HELIX a token denotes a (feature, value-bin) pair, so unlike a text token it carries ordinal meaning: a higher bin index means a larger value.

terms.gloss: Replacing a continuous value with the index of the interval it falls in.
terms.def: Splitting a continuous feature's range into intervals and replacing each value with its interval index. This is how a continuous detector quantity becomes a discrete token. Edges should be fit once and frozen so a token means the same value-range in every sample.

terms.gloss: Equal-population bins, edges placed at the data's quantiles.
terms.def: A binning strategy that places edges at the feature's quantiles, giving roughly equal event counts per bin. It uses the vocabulary efficiently but collapses on spiky/zero-inflated features, where many edges coincide and bins empty out — the collapse the occupancy metrics surface.

terms.gloss: Embeddings that respect the ordinal order of binned values (piecewise-linear / periodic).
terms.def: An embedding scheme for binned numerical features that preserves their ordering, rather than treating bins as unrelated symbols. Piecewise-linear and periodic encodings (Gorishniy 2022) let adjacent value-bins map to nearby vectors, keeping the magnitude information that plain lookup tables discard.

terms.gloss: Number of tokens per feature; the N_BINS knee sets the smallest sufficient value.
terms.def: The number of distinct tokens a feature can take (its bin count). The N_BINS sweep finds the 'knee' — the smallest vocabulary that still retains the feature's information — which directly sizes the embedding vocabulary downstream.

terms.gloss: How events spread across a feature's bins; flags collapse (empty / dominated bins).
terms.def: The distribution of events across a feature's bins. Empty bins and a single dominant bin (high max_bin_frac) indicate quantile collapse — the feature uses fewer tokens than requested. Informative rather than pass/fail: it tells you which features need fewer bins, a zero-token, or native integer tokens.

terms.gloss: mi_bin / mi_raw — the fraction of a feature's label information surviving binning.
terms.def: The ratio of binned to raw mutual information for a feature: the fraction of its label information that survives tokenization. It is the data-processing inequality measured directly; near 1.0 means binning lost essentially nothing. Robust to class imbalance because the label entropy cancels in the ratio.

terms.gloss: Rank-based separation of two classes by one variable; 0.5 = none, 1.0 = perfect.
terms.def: Area under the ROC curve, computed here as the Mann–Whitney rank statistic for one feature against the binary label, reported direction-agnostically in [0.5, 1.0]. Rank-based, so it is invariant to monotonic transforms and robust to class imbalance — which is why the gate's verdict reads separation from AUC, not from MI magnitude.

terms.gloss: Maximum gap between two empirical CDFs; a shape-based separation measure.
terms.def: The maximum vertical distance between the signal and background empirical cumulative distributions of a feature. A distribution-shape view of separation that complements the rank-based AUC.

terms.gloss: Bias correction added to plug-in entropy: +(m−1)/2N for m occupied bins, N samples.
terms.def: A first-order bias correction for the plug-in entropy estimator, which is biased low on finite samples. Adds (m−1)/2N (m = occupied bins, N = total count). Used in the histogram mutual-information estimator so low-statistics lanes do not report false information; a small residual can push retention slightly above 1.0.

terms.gloss: Text tokenization that builds a vocabulary by merging frequent character pairs.
terms.def: Byte-Pair Encoding and related schemes (WordPiece, Unigram) segment text into sub-word units whose vocabulary is learned from corpus frequency — frequent words become single tokens, rare ones fragment. The contrast with HELIX's quantization route: text tokens are nominal symbols discovered from frequency; feature tokens are ordinal symbols manufactured by binning.

terms.gloss: Per-feature single-variable separation lost when a value is replaced by its bin index.
terms.def: ΔAUC = AUC(binned) − AUC(raw), a per-feature rank-AUC difference. By the data-processing inequality it can only be ≤ 0; a positive value signals an estimator artifact or label leakage, not a gain from binning. Ranks which features tokenizing damages most.

terms.gloss: Diagnostic for tail under-resolution: how much of a feature's range one token spans.
terms.def: A per-feature geometric diagnostic on the frozen bin edges: the widest token's span as a fraction of the feature range, plus the count of edges falling in the signal region (the tail). It catches tail under-resolution — a feature can show flat occupancy and full entropy H(p_k) yet still lose mutual information because quantile binning crushed its discriminating tail into one wide token. The fifth Phase-2 metric panel; the failure mode occupancy and entropy are blind to.
